whatThePageStates: A single short availability page for one capability: AWS CloudTrail Lake. After a note that CloudTrail Lake closes to new customers on May 31, 2026, it says "Currently, CloudTrail Lake is supported in the following AWS Regions:" and gives one two-column table (Region Name, Region) with 30 data rows. Every listed row is an affirmative supported statement; the page names no unsupported Region and gives no per-Region qualifier, tier, or partial status. It closes with two pointers to CloudTrail endpoints and quotas and to GovCloud (US) service endpoints, then the standard AI-coding-assistant "See also" boilerplate.

features.statuses: 30 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 30+0+0=30. The table has 32 pipe-delimited lines: 1 header (Region Name | Region), 1 separator, and 30 data rows. Each data row is read as Yes purely by being listed under the sentence 'Currently, CloudTrail Lake is supported in the following AWS Regions'. There is no No column, no explicit exclusion sentence, and no Partial/asterisk value anywhere, so non-listed Regions are ABSENT, not stated as unsupported. The 30 rows are: us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2, af-south-1, ap-east-1, ap-south-2, ap-southeast-3, ap-southeast-4, ap-south-1, ap-northeast-3, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-northeast-1, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-south-1, eu-west-3, eu-south-2, eu-north-1, eu-central-2, il-central-1, me-south-1, me-central-1, sa-east-1, us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1.
features.scope: None. There is no second dimension: no per-plan, per-event-type, per-datastore-type, or per-feature split. The GovCloud endpoint link is a pointer, not a scope qualifier, and the May 31 2026 new-customer cutoff is a time-based commercial condition that applies uniformly to every Region rather than varying by Region.
features.reasoning: The page enumerates AWS Regions, an external universe that exists independently of CloudTrail, and the unit of claim is one Region either being on the supported list or not. The capability being claimed is CloudTrail Lake as a whole - the page never decomposes it into sub-features (event data stores, dashboards, federation, queries), so exactly one feature is on this page, not several.

shouldNotExtract: The table header row (Region Name | Region) and the markdown separator row - they are 2 of the 32 pipe lines and are not Regions. The <a name> anchor. The availability-change Note about May 31, 2026 and its link to cloudtrail-lake-service-availability-change.md - that is a lifecycle/commercial statement, not coverage. The two trailing pointer sentences to 'AWS CloudTrail endpoints and quotas' and to GovCloud 'Service Endpoints' - those are cross-links to other pages, and the endpoints/quotas page must not be counted here. The entire '## See also' block, which is the generic Agent Toolkit for AWS AI-coding-assistant boilerplate and contains no coverage. Region display names must not be counted separately from their Region codes - they are two cells of the same row, one claim.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this is the page's only dimension - 30 Regions stated supported, of which 28 are in the aws (commercial) partition and 2 (us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1) are in the aws-us-gov partition. No China (cn-*) Region appears, but their absence is silence, not a stated No. SERVICE: nothing. The page is about one service, CloudTrail, and never enumerates other AWS services; any per-service figure taken from this page is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. No resource types, event sources, event categories, or data-store types are enumerated anywhere on the page; a resource-type count from this page is fabricated.
trap: The single most likely misparse is counting 32 instead of 30 by treating the table header and separator lines as data rows - the correct answer is 30. Runners-up: (a) doubling to 60 by harvesting the Region Name cell and the Region code cell as two separate axis values; (b) inventing a 'No' population, e.g. subtracting 30 from the ~36 total AWS Regions and reporting 6 unsupported - the page states no negatives at all, so the split is 30 Yes / 0 No; (c) reading the May 31 2026 new-customer closure note as a coverage status such as Deprecated or Partial and downgrading every row; (d) chasing the linked endpoints-and-quotas or GovCloud endpoints pages and merging their Region lists into this page's count; (e) treating the GovCloud sentence as evidence of a per-partition scope dimension when the two GovCloud Regions are already plain rows in the same single table.
